issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: The truck suddenly stalls or loses power, often while working hard or towing, then cranks but won't restart. Injector warning codes may follow.
issues.why: The engine-driven high-pressure fuel pump can wear internally, especially if water or poor fuel gets in. Its metal debris then spreads through the injectors, lines and tank.
issues.next: Get the truck safely off the road and have it towed rather than cranking it over and over. Ask a diesel shop to check the fuel filters for metal. Keeping water out of the fuel and changing filters on time lowers the risk.

issues.t: Oil cooler and EGR cooler failure leading to head gasket trouble
issues.sym: White, sweet-smelling exhaust smoke, coolant that keeps going down with no visible leak, coolant pushing out of the overflow bottle, and running hot when loaded.
issues.why: The oil cooler can clog inside and starve the EGR cooler of coolant. The EGR cooler then cracks and leaks coolant into the exhaust, and the extra heat and pressure can lift the head gaskets on this engine.
issues.next: Stop towing or hauling and have a diesel shop compare oil and coolant temperatures and pressure-test the cooling system. Catching a clogged oil cooler early can save a far larger head gasket job.

issues.t: EGR cooler failure and coolant blowing out of the reservoir
issues.sym: Coolant spits out of the coolant reservoir, mostly when hauling a load or with the A/C on. Coolant level drops and the truck may run hot or puff white smoke.
issues.why: This engine has two EGR coolers, and the first one in line often cracks from heat. Owners also report head gasket failures that let combustion pressure into the cooling system.
issues.next: Don't keep working the truck while it is losing coolant. A diesel shop can pressure-test the cooling system and check the EGR coolers. Many of these repairs need the cab lifted off, so get a written estimate first.

issues.t: Radiator leaks at the plastic tank seam
issues.sym: A coolant puddle under the front of the truck, a sweet smell, and a coolant level that keeps dropping. The leak is often at the seam along the side of the radiator.
issues.why: The radiator's plastic end tanks can separate from the aluminum core, especially as the truck ages and sees heavy heat cycles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level before every trip and watch the temperature gauge. Have the radiator inspected; a leaking one should be replaced before it fails on the road. A coolant puddle on this engine is more often the radiator than a head gasket.

issues.t: Fuel tank lining flakes and clogs the fuel system
issues.sym: The truck bogs, loses power under load or stalls, and fuel filters clog again soon after being changed. Fuel samples may show silver or rusty flakes.
issues.why: The inside of the steel fuel tank can break down and shed flakes. The debris clogs filters and can damage the fuel pump and injectors.
issues.next: If filters keep clogging, ask the shop to drain a fuel sample and inspect the tank before replacing more parts. A new tank plus fresh filters is usually needed; check whether any warranty or goodwill help applies.

issues.t: Injector control module (FICM) failure
issues.sym: Hard starting or no start, especially in cold weather, rough running, misfires and stalling.
issues.why: The module that powers the injectors can lose voltage as its internal parts wear, often made worse by weak batteries. Without enough voltage the injectors don't fire properly.
issues.next: Test both batteries first, since weak batteries strain the module. A diesel shop can check the module's output voltage. A rebuilt module with a warranty is a common fix.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough or choppy idle, hard starting, sudden stalling while driving, or a crank-but-no-start. A warning light may or may not come on.
issues.why: The camshaft sensor tells the computer when to fire the injectors. When it fails, even for a moment, the engine can quit.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Ford recalled this sensor on 7.3L diesel trucks. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Spark plug blown out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking from the engine, a rough run with a flashing check engine light, and sometimes an ignition coil sitting loose on top.
issues.why: The early two-valve V10 holds each spark plug with only a few threads in the aluminum head. A plug can loosen over time and strip out of the head.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine suddenly starts popping and misfiring. A shop can usually repair the threads with an insert. Make sure plugs are tightened correctly at every tune-up.

issues.t: Spark plugs seize and break during removal
issues.sym: No symptom while driving. The trouble shows up at a tune-up, when plugs break during removal and leave part of the plug stuck in the head.
issues.why: The three-valve V10 uses a two-piece plug that can carbon up and seize. Ford issued a bulletin with a special removal and extraction procedure.
issues.next: Have plugs changed by a shop that knows Ford's procedure for this engine. Ask for an estimate that covers extraction in case a plug breaks.

issues.t: Exhaust manifold studs break, causing a ticking exhaust leak
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from the engine area, loudest on a cold start, sometimes with an exhaust smell in the cab or a check engine light.
issues.why: The small studs holding the exhaust manifolds to the V10 heads rust and snap after years of heat and road salt, letting exhaust leak at the joint.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm which studs are broken. Don't wait too long, since leaking exhaust can burn nearby wiring and a leak near the cab is unsafe. Stronger studs and anti-seize help prevent a repeat.

issues.t: Fuel in the oil from soot filter cleaning cycles
issues.sym: The oil level rises on the dipstick, oil smells like diesel, and the truck may regenerate its soot filter often, with a hot exhaust smell after short trips.
issues.why: To burn soot out of the filter, the engine sprays extra fuel. Some of that fuel washes past the rings into the oil, thinning it.
issues.next: Check the dipstick often and change oil about every 5,000 miles. If the oil level keeps climbing, have a diesel shop check for a clogged soot filter or a leaking injector.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure on early 6.7L diesels
issues.sym: A loud screech or whine from the engine, blue-gray smoke from the tailpipe and loss of power.
issues.why: Early turbos on this engine used ceramic bearings that could fail. Ford later switched to steel bearings.
issues.next: Stop and shut the engine off if you hear a sudden screech with smoke. Have a diesel shop inspect the turbo before oil loss damages the engine.

issues.t: Exhaust temperature sensor fault can shut the engine off (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, or won't restart, with an exhaust temperature fault. Ambulance and fire-truck chassis were most affected.
issues.why: A false exhaust temperature sensor reading can make the computer shut the engine down to protect it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls, especially on ambulance or emergency vehicles. If the engine shuts off, steer to safety and call for service.

issues.t: Fuel line connector can separate and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the truck.
issues.why: A fuel jumper line was made with the wrong end shape, so it can pull apart and leak fuel near hot parts.
issues.next: Don't drive if you smell raw fuel. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the line replaced.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or stalls while driving, may not restart, and may set a check engine light.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump on gas engines can fail, cutting fuel to the engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the pump free.

issues.t: Fuel pump deposits can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power, hard starting or a stall while driving.
issues.why: Deposits from biodiesel blends can build up in the high-pressure fuel pump and make it fail. Some trucks fixed under the first recall were repaired incorrectly and were recalled again.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for both recalls. If the truck stalls, steer to safety and have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Violent front-end shake ('death wobble')
issues.sym: After hitting a bump or rough patch, usually above 45 mph, the steering wheel and front end shake violently and keep shaking until you slow way down.
issues.why: The solid front axle can start to oscillate when the track bar, ball joints, tie rods or steering damper are worn or loose, or alignment is off. Often more than one part contributes.
issues.next: Slow down gently without slamming the brakes; the shaking stops at low speed. Have a shop inspect the whole front end, not just the steering damper, since a new damper alone can hide the real cause.

issues.t: Steering wheel shake after bumps (steering damper program)
issues.sym: The steering wheel keeps oscillating after hitting rough pavement, usually above about 45 mph.
issues.why: Ford found the steering linkage damper on these trucks may not control front-end oscillation well enough, and set up a program to replace it on all F-450 and F-550 trucks of these years.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer whether program 20N04 has been done on your truck. Slow down gently if the shaking starts.

issues.t: Steering gear can bind or lose steering (recall)
issues.sym: Noise from the steering box, steering that feels notchy or stiff, or loss of steering.
issues.why: Some steering gears on chassis-cab trucks were built with the wrong retainer for an internal ball tube.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for open recalls right away. Don't drive if steering feels unusual.

issues.t: Steering column shaft bolts may be loose or missing (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or looseness in the steering, or steering that stops responding.
issues.why: Bolts that join the upper steering shaft may have been left loose or left out at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Don't drive if steering feels loose. NHTSA recall number: 23V-344.

issues.t: Front wheel hub extenders may be loose and a wheel can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a front wheel, vibration, or a wheel that wobbles. Dual-rear-wheel trucks use these hub extenders.
issues.why: The fasteners holding the front hub extenders may not have been tightened properly, so the front wheel can loosen and separate.
issues.next: Ford advised owners not to drive until the nuts are checked. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer inspect them. NHTSA recall number: 23V-758.

issues.t: Driveline vibration can break the driveline or transmission (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration at highway speeds, noises from under the truck, and in the worst case a loss of drive power.
issues.why: Vibration in the driveline at highway speed can crack the driveline or transmission parts on F-450 and F-550 trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you feel new vibration from under the truck, slow down and have it inspected. NHTSA recall number: 17V-212.

issues.t: Brake pedal pushrod can disconnect (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal goes to the floor or feels disconnected, with sudden loss of braking.
issues.why: A retaining spring on the brake booster pushrod may be missing, so the pushrod can slip off the brake pedal.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away and don't drive an affected truck until it is inspected.

issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, sometimes with the engine off, or cruise control that stops working.
issues.why: A pressure switch on the brake system that turns off cruise control can leak internally, overheat and start an underhood fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls right away. Park outdoors away from buildings until it is fixed.

issues.t: Turn signals and brake lights may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals, hazard lights, tail lights or brake lights don't come on.
issues.why: A small slider inside the steering column multi-function switch can deform, so the lights it controls stop working.
issues.next: Check your lights and your VIN for open recalls. Have the switch replaced; other drivers can't see you stop or turn without these lights.

issues.t: PTO pressure switch can leak oil onto the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: A burning-oil smell or smoke from under the truck on chassis cabs fitted with a power take-off for dump bodies, cranes or aerial lifts.
issues.why: On some upfitted trucks with a Muncie power take-off, the pressure switch can leak oil onto the exhaust heat blanket, which can catch fire.
issues.next: These recalls come from the body builders, not Ford. Check your VIN and body builder's tag for open recalls and look for oil around the PTO.

issues.t: Engine block heater cord can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A melted or scorched block heater cord or plug, a burning smell after plugging in, or no engine heat on cold mornings.
issues.why: The block heater cord splice can let in water and corrode, then overheat and melt.
issues.next: Stop using the block heater until it is checked. Check your VIN for open recalls. NHTSA recall number: 19V-278.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioner sparks can start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash. After a crash where the front seat belts tighten, smoke or fire can start near the door pillars in crew-cab trucks.
issues.why: When the front belt pretensioner fires, its hot gases can ignite carpet or insulation in the pillar area.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls on crew-cab trucks. The fix adds heat shielding. NHTSA recall number: 19V-880.

issues.t: Backup camera image may be blank, distorted or upside down (recall)
issues.sym: The screen shows a blank, distorted or upside-down picture when shifting into reverse.
issues.why: A fault in the camera can make it send a bad image.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and back up carefully using mirrors until it is fixed. NHTSA recall numbers: 22V-644, 25V-572.

issues.t: Backup camera may freeze, lag or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is late, frozen, blank or distorted when backing up.
issues.why: Camera hardware and software faults can keep the image from showing correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; most are fixed with a free software update. NHTSA recall numbers: 24V-806, 25V-315.

issues.t: Windshield wiper arms may break (recall)
issues.sym: One or both wipers stop moving or flop loose, often in heavy rain or snow.
issues.why: The wiper arms can crack or break under load.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Avoid driving in rain or snow with a broken wiper. NHTSA recall number: 26V-204.

issues.t: Trailer brake module can lose connection while towing (recall)
issues.sym: A trailer warning message, trailer brakes or trailer lights that stop working while towing.
issues.why: The built-in trailer module can lose communication with the truck, cutting trailer brakes or lights.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls before towing. If the warning appears, slow down and stop safely. NHTSA recall number: 26V-104.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy due to clock spring fault (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may be on.
issues.why: A clock spring inside the steering wheel may have a bad weld that disconnects the driver airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get it fixed promptly. NHTSA recall number: 23V-847.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may fail or gauges read wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge cluster stays dark at startup, or the speedometer and tachometer stick or jump around.
issues.why: Some clusters have a fault that stops them from starting up, and some analog clusters can move erratically.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for open recalls. Don't rely on the speedometer until it is fixed.

issues.t: LED headlights may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Part of a headlight goes dark.
issues.why: A contaminated LED chip inside the headlight can fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and avoid night driving with a failed headlight.
